root_cause_description: Increased mechanical friction at one robot axis joint or gearbox, requiring higher motor torque to maintain the commanded trajectory. Simulates dirt or age-related gear wear.
error_description: Friction model

root_cause_description: The motor commutation phase is deliberately offset in firmware, reducing torque-forming efficiency without affecting the commanded path or velocity. Simulates electrical or magnetic component wear.
error_description: Max current deviation failure
error_suggestion: a) Do a Complete rebooting sequence. b) If this happens more than two times in a row, replace joint

root_cause_description: A physical weight is attached to one robot axis, increasing its effective inertia and gravity loading. Affects torque demands on all joints due to the kinematic chain.
error_description: (base)
error_suggestion: Check payload, center of gravity and acceleration settings. Log screen may contain additional information.

root_cause_description: The robot contacts a soft foam block placed in the workspace. The low stiffness of foam absorbs most of the impact energy, producing a brief TCP force spike and transient torque perturbation without triggering a protective stop.
error_description: Protective Stop: Collision detected by joint

root_cause_description: A cable is attached along the robot arm with cable ties, introducing pose-dependent friction and gravity loading on affected axes as the cable bends and twists during motion.
error_description: Robot motion causes too high joint torques on Shoulder.
error_suggestion: Review your accelerations, blends and if there are collisions or excessive torques in the joint, adjust accordingly.

root_cause_description: The robot's mounting platform is unstable due to released wheel brakes or uneven foam placement beneath it, introducing low-frequency vibrations into the arm during motion. Conceptually related to fixture_instability (fault_id 11) but applies to the robot base rather than the workpiece.
error_description: Robot motion causes too high joint torques on Base.
error_suggestion: Review your accelerations, blends and if there are collisions or excessive torques in the joint, adjust accordingly.

root_cause_description: Joint gearbox is operating close to its shear torque limit due to excessive acceleration, deceleration, or mechanical obstruction.
error_description: Close to gearbox shear limit
error_explanation: Acceleration/deceleration to high. Mechanical problem in gear related to encoder mounting
error_suggestion: a) Reduce acceleration in user program. b) Do a Complete rebooting sequence. c) If this happens more than several times in a row, replace joint

root_cause_description: Motor is receiving current commands but the encoder reports no position change, indicating a stalled or seized motor shaft.
error_description: Motor encoder error

root_cause_description: A joint exceeded its maximum allowable speed, triggering safety system intervention. Can result from incorrect trajectory planning or encoder miscalibration.
error_description: Max joint-encoder speed exceeded
error_suggestion: a) Do a Complete rebooting sequence. b) If this happens more than two times in a row, replace joint

root_cause_description: Robot joint moved outside its configured soft or hard position limits, triggering a safety stop.
error_description: Max motor-encoder speed exceeded
error_suggestion: a) Do a Complete rebooting sequence. b) If this happens more than two times in a row, replace joint

root_cause_description: Robot is drawing significantly more power than expected during idle state, indicating an internal electrical fault, short circuit, or brake malfunction.
error_description: Idle power consumption to high
error_explanation: The system is drawing more power than expected while idle
error_suggestion: a) Check Energy Eaters cables and connections b) Check Energy Eater c) Replace Energy Eater

root_cause_description: The programmed trajectory passes through or very close to a kinematic singularity (wrist or shoulder), causing the controller to halt linear motion and issue a protective stop.
error_description: Protective Stop: Position in singularity
error_explanation: Robot cannot move linear near a singularity
error_suggestion: Use Move J or change the motion

root_cause_description: The Tool Center Point (TCP) frame or mounting orientation is configured incorrectly in PolyScope, causing the robot to detect unexpected gravitational torques consistent with wrong mounting.
error_description: Protective Stop: Wrong payload or mounting detected, or something is pushing the robot when entering Free drive mode
error_explanation: The robot may move unexpected due to wrong settings
error_suggestion: Verify that the TCP configuration and mounting in the used installation is correct

root_cause_description: The payload mass is left at 0 kg in the robot configuration while a tool or workpiece is physically attached, causing the collision detection model to trigger on normal inertial forces.
error_description: Protective Stop: Collision detected by joint
error_explanation: The joint torque model detected an unexpected resistive force consistent with a physical collision while the payload is specified as 0 kg, making the collision threshold very sensitive.
error_suggestion: a) Set the correct payload mass and center of gravity in the installation settings. b) Clear any obstruction from the workspace. c) Verify acceleration and speed settings are appropriate for the mounted tool.

root_cause_description: The robot trajectory crosses a configured safety plane or zone boundary, triggering an immediate protective stop from the safety system.
error_description: Protective Stop: Position close to safety plane limits
error_explanation: The robot TCP or a body link has approached or crossed a configured safety plane boundary defined in the safety configuration.
error_suggestion: a) Review safety plane positions in the safety configuration. b) Modify the robot program to keep all motion within the defined safety zones. c) Check that the correct safety configuration is active.

root_cause_description: An external force continuously pulls or pushes the robot arm during motion, such as a tethered cable, hanging weight, or operator interference, causing persistent torque anomalies.
error_description: Something is pulling the robot
error_suggestion: Check TCP configuration, payload and mounting settings

root_cause_description: The absolute magnetic encoder read head is physically displaced relative to the magnetic ring — due to mechanical shock, loose mounting, or external magnetic interference — causing invalid position decoding.
error_description: Invalid decode: Read head misalignment, ring damaged or external magnetic field present.
error_explanation: Magnetic encoder error (absolute encoder) . Argument = sum of C 74 errors
error_suggestion: Check grounding and shielding for EMC problems

root_cause_description: One or more motor phase wires are partially or fully disconnected at the joint connector, reducing available torque and causing asymmetric current draw across phases.
error_description: Phase 3 or multiple phases is unconnected or not working
error_explanation: The wire is (1) damaged or (2) has been disconnected from the PCB(not likely) or (3) defect PCB
error_suggestion: a) Check joint for damaged or loose connections. b) Replace the joint

root_cause_description: The payload center of gravity (CoG) is specified at an incorrect offset from the tool flange, causing the gravity compensation model to apply wrong torques and triggering protective stops during motion.
error_description: The protective stop was likely caused by incorrectly specified payload mass and/or center of gravity.
error_explanation: Specifying an incorrect payload mass and/or center of gravity may cause poor robot performance and/or protective stops.
error_suggestion: Make sure the specified payload mass and center of gravity are correct.

root_cause_description: A cable or wire hangs across the robot workspace and contacts the arm or tool during motion. The flexible cable wraps around or drags along the arm, producing a sustained asymmetric pull force and persistent torque anomaly rather than a sharp impact.
error_description: Protective Stop: Collision detected by joint

root_cause_description: The robot strikes a cardboard carton or flat-pack box placed in its path. Cardboard provides moderate resistance — the robot may displace the object or, if the carton is braced, generate enough torque deviation to trigger a protective stop.
error_description: Protective Stop: Collision detected by joint

root_cause_description: The robot collides with a hard, immovable object such as a metal fixture, tool stand, or structural element. The high contact stiffness produces an immediate large torque deviation and invariably triggers a protective stop.
error_description: Protective Stop: Collision detected by joint
